w: Bronze Age burial mounds crown the summit, and on a clear day you can see across the Bristol Channel to Weston-super-Mare and north to Pen y Fan. Its sister hill, the Lesser Garth, was quarried away almost to nothing for limestone. Below, abandoned coal mines once fed the valley's ironworks.
s: Burial mounds on a hill quarried nearly out of existence
_facts: Bronze Age burial mounds (tumuli) sit on its summit
Visible from nearly all of Cardiff and the Taff Valley; on a clear day sightlines reach Weston-super-Mare and Pen y Fan
Its limestone sister hill, the Lesser Garth, has been extensively quarried and mined for iron ore
19th-century coal mines on its lower slopes fed ironworks in the Taff valley

w: Cardiff's grandest park was reclaimed from what locals called a malarial bog -- 130 acres of it, dammed into a 30-acre lake you can walk right around in a mile and a bit. Four islands shelter nesting water birds, and rowing boats still work the water the Victorians engineered from a stream called the Nant Fawr.
s: A Victorian park engineered out of a malarial bog
_facts: Built on 130 acres of reclaimed bogland historically known as a malarial bog
Includes a 30-acre lake, 1.3 miles around, formed by damming the Nant Fawr stream
Has four islands within a conservation area that are home to water birds
Awarded the Green Flag award for park quality

w: More than forty buildings -- cottages, a chapel, ironworkers' terraces -- were dismantled across Wales and rebuilt here, brick by brick, around a Grade I listed Elizabethan manor. Which? once crowned it the nation's favourite visitor attraction; a six-year, £30m rebuild later won it Art Fund Museum of the Year.
s: A whole country's buildings, dismantled and rebuilt here
_facts: Open-air museum with more than forty re-erected buildings from locations across Wales
Set in the grounds of St Fagans Castle, a Grade I listed Elizabethan manor house
Named UK's favourite visitor attraction by Which? magazine in 2011
A six-year, £30 million revamp completed in 2018 led to Art Fund Museum of the Year in 2019
